subject: Re: [stan-users] Jacobian correction needed for including measurement rounding error?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Jacobian correction needed for including measurement rounding error?
parts:
No, becuase you're putting priors on the parameters, not
on transformed parameters.

You only need Jacobians when you transform a parameter
and then put a distribution on the transformed parameter.

parameters {
real a;
real b;
...
model {
(1 / a) ~ gamma(b, b); // needs Jacobian

parameters {
real a;
real b;
...
model {
a ~ gamma(1 / b, 1 / b); // no Jacobian necessary

- Bob


> On Apr 12, 2017, at 1:07 PM, dy...@backyardbrains.com wrote:
>
> Hello!
>
> I'm creating a model where I want to account for rounding error of measurements, following the model on page 198 of the user’s guide, but I'm also scaling the data in order to implement weakly informed priors. Do I need to make any additional Jacobian corrections above and beyond those in the manual to account for the additional scaling?
>
>
> data {
> int nSubj ;
> int nY ;
> int nB ;
> vector[nY] Y ;
> matrix[nSubj,nB] B ;
> }
> parameters {
> vector[nB] scaled_coef_means ;
> real<lower=0> scaled_int_sds ;
> vector<lower=-0.5, upper=0.5>[nY] E;
> }
> transformed parameters{
> vector[nY] Y_scaled ;
> Y_scaled = ((Y+E)-mean(Y))/sd(Y) ;
> }
> model {
> scaled_coef_means ~ normal(0,1) ;
> scaled_int_sds ~ weibull(2,1) ;
> }
> generated quantities{
> vector[nB] coef_means ;
> real int_sds ;
> int_sds = scaled_int_sds * sd(Y) ;
> coef_means = scaled_coef_means * sd(Y) ;
> coef_means[1] = coef_means[1] + mean(Y) ;
> }
>
> Thanks!
